name: GarmentCode
description: A modular programming framework for designing parametric sewing patterns
readme_summary: GarmentCode is a Python framework for designing parametric sewing patterns. It provides a library (PyGarment) for defining garment components and their relationships, enabling the creation of customizable and adaptable clothing designs. The project also includes a dataset of 3D garments and a configurator GUI for interactive design.
key_features: Modular programming framework for parametric sewing patterns
PyGarment core library with base types and operators
Design of garment components and interfaces
Support for body measurements and design presets
primary_use_case: Designing and generating parametric sewing patterns for customizable garments.
cover_image_prompt: A master tailor in a futuristic workshop, using a holographic interface to sculpt a 3D garment from flowing digital fabric. The tailor's hands gesture, and the fabric transforms, showing intricate seams and panels being precisely defined. On one side, a blueprint displays parametric controls and body measurements, while on the other, a perfectly formed garment emerges. Subtle code snippets and data streams flow around the scene, indicating the underlying programming. The overall mood is one of creative precision and digital craftsmanship, rendered in a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with a palette of blues, whites, and subtle gold accents. The repository name 'GarmentCode' is subtly integrated into the holographic display.

name: effectcraft
description: EffectCraft: An open-source motion graphics and compositing tool written by scratch in pure Rust
readme_summary: EffectCraft is an open-source motion graphics and compositing tool written in Rust, aiming to be a clean-room reimplementation of Adobe After Effects. It offers features like Lottie import/export, scriptability, and a readable project file format, making it suitable for creating animated titles, motion graphics, and visual effects.
key_features: Cross-platform (macOS, Windows, Linux) and web support
primary_use_case: Creating motion graphics, visual effects, and animated titles.
cover_image_prompt: A master clockmaker meticulously assembling intricate gears and springs, representing the core components of motion graphics. Instead of traditional clock parts, the gears are stylized digital icons for layers, keyframes, and effects. A glowing blueprint of the 'EffectCraft' logo is visible on the workbench, with streams of digital light flowing from the clockmaker's tools into a central, animated scene displayed on a holographic screen. The scene should convey precision, creativity, and the transformation of raw elements into dynamic visuals. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a vibrant color palette.

name: pipedream
description: Connect APIs, remarkably fast.  Free for developers.
readme_summary: Pipedream is a developer-focused integration platform that enables the creation of event-driven automations by connecting various applications. It offers pre-built components for over 1,000 integrations and supports custom code in Node.js, Python, Golang, and Bash for complex logic.
key_features: Workflows: Sequences of steps (pre-built actions or custom code) triggered by events.
Event Sources: Triggers for workflows, emitting events from services like GitHub, Slack, and Airtable.
Actions: Pre-built code steps for performing common operations across integrated apps.
Custom Code: Support for Node.js, Python, Golang, and Bash for custom logic.
Integrations: Over 1,000 pre-built integrations with popular applications.
primary_use_case: Building event-driven automations and integrating disparate applications through a low-code platform with custom code capabilities.
cover_image_prompt: A vibrant, bustling digital marketplace where various application icons (like Slack, Google Sheets, GitHub) are represented as stalls. A central, friendly robot character, labeled 'Pipedream', is expertly weaving glowing threads of data between these stalls, seamlessly connecting them. Input data streams, visualized as colorful packets, flow into the robot, and are transformed into organized outputs that reach their destination stalls. Subtle UI elements showing workflow steps and code snippets are integrated into the background. The scene is rendered in a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with bright, optimistic lighting and a clear, uncluttered composition.

name: jarm
readme_summary: JARM is a Python-based tool for active Transport Layer Security (TLS) server fingerprinting. It generates unique fingerprints for TLS servers by analyzing their responses to a series of Client Hello packets, enabling verification of TLS configurations, grouping of servers by configuration, identification of default infrastructure, and detection of malicious command and control servers.
key_features: Detects malware command and control infrastructure
Command-line interface for single or batch runs
primary_use_case: Identifying and grouping TLS servers on the internet based on their unique TLS configurations, with applications in security, infrastructure analysis, and threat detection.
cover_image_prompt: A digital alchemist in a dimly lit laboratory, meticulously analyzing glowing, intricate lock mechanisms (representing TLS server responses). The alchemist is carefully placing fragments of these locks into a central crucible, where they merge and transform into a single, unique, crystalline fingerprint. Subtle data streams flow from various servers depicted as distant, glowing nodes in the background, feeding into the alchemist's analysis. The JARM logo is subtly etched onto the alchemist's workbench. The scene should evoke a sense of precise analysis and discovery, rendered in a detailed, slightly mystical digital painting style with a focus on glowing elements and intricate details.
